mappings.parent_claim_text: The frozen literature supports genus-two octagon objects, Bolza context, and length-spectrum candidate generation but does not by itself identify unique primitive inverse-paired owners.
The control nonarithmeticity and Bolza systolic context remain bounded multi-source and inherited project inputs rather than a new exact Phase-6 proof or an unqualified single-source theorem claim.
The certificate architecture may use two sound surface-specific exact proof producers, provided both emit one common semantic owner-certificate schema that an independent validator checks.

The common semantic schema must distinguish full-group conjugacy, maximal-root and primitivity evidence, external inversion pairing, self-reciprocity, repetition accounting, termination, and positive or negative replay payloads.

At the frozen cutoff, the target side is largely constrained by the inherited systolic-empty replay while the nontrivial prospective owner closure lies on the control side; this asymmetry limits the scientific comparison claim.

P33-RC-1 remains a fail-closed certificate-methods gate whose obligations can be organized by producer-specific soundness, common-schema interoperability, and independent validation rather than one shared implementation.

The report's contribution is an interoperable exact-certificate methods design for a frozen target/control pair, not a completed census, magnetic comparison, novelty claim, or between-surface arithmetic result.
Phase-6 revision changes no scientific census, formal Route-A tuple, A0 prohibition, positive arithmetic A2 status, Route-B status, project claim, or canonical manuscript result.
